summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and HIV presented with a partially dislodged right femoral dialysis catheter, preventing her scheduled dialysis. She also reported nontraumatic pain in her left first and second toes. Imaging showed no fracture, and the pain was managed symptomatically. The dialysis catheter was successfully exchanged over the wire the night of admission without complications. Hemodialysis was completed the following day, and she was discharged home in stable condition. She was counseled on the importance of adhering to her HIV medication regimen, though she expressed a preference to take her medications at home. Follow-up was advised for persistent toe pain and routine care with her primary and specialty providers.
